analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. The only change is in docs/architecture/inference.md, head lines 595-611. It describes a Gated DeltaNet prefill kernel selection for the qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. On first use of each kernel instantiation, the process probes the packed kernel and then the rows kernel. It keeps the first one that reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit, and otherwise falls back to the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows always use the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED can force a kernel for A/B measurement.

I checked this against T-041/SEC-035 (prefix-cache scoping and checkpoint capture), TB-007 (inference engine) and T-007/T-027 (output integrity). The docs claim that mixing kernels cannot change recurrent checkpoint state, because a selected kernel matches the stock kernel bit for bit. Cache scope, salt and HMAC naming are untouched. No authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data-exposure behavior changes.

Two points remain unverified, because the source is not supplied:
- The bit-exactness guarantee covers only the fixed probe window, not every input. Divergence on other windows could cause checkpoint restore mismatches, which is a correctness/availability concern rather than a cross-tenant one.
- The env override can force a non-validated packed or rows kernel. Operators already control the binary environment (ADV-001), so this adds no new trust.

The rest of the excerpt (Nemotron Super and GLM sections) is unchanged surrounding text. No security regression was identified.
